analysis: Examined StartupPreloader.swift (base and head) and the new ModelCalibrationTests test. The preloader change adds an optional `shapeWarmup` closure to Dependencies (head lines 55-58, 92, 105). It is invoked after a successful load, either with no self-test (head 188-191) or after a passing self-test (head 198-199). A failed self-test never reaches the warmup. With selfTestFailClosed, the model is retired before any warmup, so the fail-closed semantics are preserved. Cancellation breaks the loop as before. Memory admission, the live required-GB check, the canLoadMore gate and the insufficient-memory log redaction are unchanged. The closure is injected and defaults to nil, so there is no new input from the coordinator, consumers or providers. The preloader makes no network call and handles no keys or attestation. The warmup closure itself is not in the supplied evidence. Its implementation (likely in ProviderLoop+StartupPreload or EngineV2Bridge) could in principle touch the prefix cache (T-041), billing counters, or telemetry, and could consume GPU memory beyond the admission check (T-029). The next pass should confirm that the warmup is excluded from billing and generation totals, does not donate to or probe the SSD prefix cache with prompts that are persisted to disk, uses synthetic prompts, is bounded in time and memory, and does not delay the coordinator connection indefinitely. The test-only change adds promptSizingIsMaximal in ModelCalibrationTests (head 350-367). It has no production security impact and only checks that calibration prompt sizing is maximal. No regression against the threat model was identified in the supplied units. Remaining uncertainty is limited to the unseen warmup implementation and the wiring that sets shapeWarmup.
